sentence: This is a 52-year-old male patient with a medical history of controlled arterial hypertension and stage V chronic kidney disease of 6 years of evolution on hemodialysis 3 times a week who began the disease when he presented with lower incisor odontalgia, dysphagia, odynophagia, increased volume in the painful submandibular region and local hyperthermia, which is why the patient goes to the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Unit of the Hospital General del Oeste "Dr. José Gregorio Hernández" (CBMF-HGO); 24 h later, given the patient's systemic clinical conditions and presenting leukocytosis of 27,800 U/mm3, with neutrophilia of 82.4% and creatinine at 7.5 mg/dl, it was decided to admit him.
The physical examination revealed icteric sclerae, a severe increase in volume with predominance of the bilateral submental and submandibular region, and mouth opening limited to approximately 15 mm.

The intraoral examination revealed partial maxillomandibular edentulism, generalized chronic periodontal disease with grade IV mobility of 3.1 and 4.1, presence of local irritants, halitosis, severe increase in the volume of the floor of the mouth and bilateral sublingual space with glossoptosis. .

In conjunction with the Infectious Diseases and Internal Medicine services, empirical treatment was initiated with crystalline sodium penicillin 4,000,000 IU every 6 hours intravenously and aztreonam 1 g intravenously on a daily basis.

Computed tomography is indicated, which shows an isodense image in the parapharyngeal space compatible with an increase in volume, showing a decrease in the lumen of the airways in the cervical region and corroborating the diagnosis of Ludwig's angina.
In 10 days of treatment the evolution was torpid.
A reassessment by infectology was performed, which indicated vancomycin 1 g intravenously, a drug that caused significant clinical improvement in the patient.

After systemic stabilization of the patient, a 3.1 and 4.1 extraction is performed and surgical drainage of the sublingual, submandibular and submental spaces is achieved through a bilateral submental and submandibular incision inferior to the mandibular basal area that allows access , communication and establishment of 3 passive drainages with a Nellaton catheter to perform 3 daily saline washes for 3 weeks.
In the evolution after surgical drainage and replacement of antibiotic therapy, the patient presented a decrease in the increase in volume and a stabilization of the respiratory rate.
The last hematology recorded revealed a white series of 8,600 U/mm3, at the expense of neutrophils (78%), hemoglobin of 9.5 g/dl, hematocrit of 32.7% and creatinine of 6.8 mg/dl.
All of these conditions led to a medical discharge.
